messages.subject: anchor item in add_sequential DIF detection
parts:
Hi Phil,

I'm using mirt to test a scale for DIF. I'm using the add sequential scheme and want to be sure I'm identifying my baseline model correctly (code below). I did not enter an anchor item into the "invariance" argument of multiGroup because I am thinking that the purification process performed by the "add_sequential" scheme results in anchor items in each iteration--but I'm not sure if I'm thinking of this correctly and perhaps am identifying my baseline model incorrectly? Any thoughts are appreciated. Thank you! 



mod <- multipleGroup(data = sf.dif[,c("sf1", "sf23", "sf4", "sf5")], 1, 
                                        itemtype = c("2PL", "graded", "2PL", "2PL"), group = as.character(sf.dif[,5]), 
                                        invariance = c('free_means', 'free_var'), SE.type = "Oakes", SE = TRUE)

sf.add.seq <- DIF(mod, c('a', "d", "d1", "d2"), scheme = 'add_sequential', p.adjust = 'BH', seq_stat = .05, plotdif = TRUE) 
print(sf.add.seq)

-Jeannie

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: anchor item in add_sequential DIF detection
parts:
Hi Jeannie,

You would need to have at least one item's name in the invariance= input to specify an anchor item, otherwise the baseline model will not be sufficiently identified. But, one item is pretty weak in that if you happen to pick an anchor that has DIF then it can throw the results of the search off. I think the common number of anchors in the literature starts with three items, but the more the better. HTH.

Phil

Hi Phil, I'm reading your 2016 paper "It might not make a big DIF..." (it is awesome by the way). I'd like to use the method you discuss for evaluating DIF but want to be sure I'm translating your method to its programming in mirt correctly. I've copied and pasted your methods and the coding for each step below. Does this look right to you? (this example assumes the test is 10 items and has 5-point response cats). Thank you so much!

1. "To establish a set of potential anchor items, we used a multigroup GRM with no across-group equality constraints as a reference model. 
    mod1 <- multipleGroup(data = df[,c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "x5", "x6", "x7, "x8", "x9", "x10")], 1, itemtype = "graded", group = as.character(df[,11]), invariance = c('free_means', 'free_var'), SE = TRUE)
2. "Next, likelihood-ratio tests were used to compare the reference model to models that added across-group equality constraints to the a and dk parameters one item at a time. To account for the large number of likelihood ratio tests, we used the multiplicity control method of Benjamini and Hochberg (1995). Based on the DIF analysis, we determined that the third, sixth, seventh, and eighth items were invariant across the two countries. "

dif <- DIF(mod1, c('a', "d1", "d2", "d3", "d4"), scheme = 'add_sequential',  p.adjust = 'BH', seq_stat = .01)

3. "Therefore, these items were used as anchor items in the final multigroup IRT model so that the latent mean and variance parameters in the German group could be estimated. A likelihood-ratio test comparing our final model to a multigroup IRT model with no across-group equality constraints was not statistically significant."
    mod2 <- multipleGroup(data = df[,"x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "x5", "x6", "x7, "x8", "x9", "x10")], 1, itemtype = "graded", group = as.character(df[,11]), invariance = c('x3', 'x6', 'x7', 'x8', 'free_means', 'free_var'), SE = TRUE)
    dif2 <- DIF(mod2, c('a', "d1", "d2", "d3", "d4"), scheme = 'drop',  items2test = c(1:2,4:5,9:10))
Thank you again! -Jeannie

Correct.

Phil

Otherwise, you are making the strong assumption that the latent traits have identical distribution properties, which if false will lead to incorrect identification of DIF.

The 0x0 data frame mean that given the first was of DIF searching no DIF items were found according to the selection criteria. HTH.

Phil

Hi Phil, hope all is well. Do you happen to know of a citation(s) for the comment you mentioned where even if the wrong anchor items are chosen, the composite should still show response bias in the test as a whole? This would be super helpful for me to cite in the work i'm doing.

thanks!
Keri
On Fri, Sep 6, 2019 at 12:29 PM Phil Chalmers <rphilip....@gmail.com> wrote:

Yes, everything in your code looks fine, but again I think the best practice is to use anchor items first. The process described in the DTF paper isn't completely kosher, but then interest was less about DIF and more about the aggregate DTF effects. For DTF, even if the wrong anchor items are chosen (and therefore alternative items end up showing DIF) the composite still should show response bias in the test as a whole. 

Regarding the output from the DIF() function, I recall that there was some weird bug that appears on the current CRAN version that has been patched on the Github dev. Feel free to install that first and check again, though I am planning on releasing a new version of mirt next week. Cheers.

Phil


On Thu, Sep 5, 2019 at 3:09 PM Jeannie <jeann...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Phil, the first warning I just ignored because I am trying to use your method of DIF detection. So I only ran the multiGroup model without freeing the latent mean/variance (and without anchor items) to identify anchors using this code:
mod1 <- multipleGroup(data = df[,c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "x5", "x6", "x7, "x8", "x9", "x10")], 1, itemtype = "graded", group = as.character(df[,11]), SE = TRUE)

dif1 <- DIF(mod1, c('a', "d1", "d2", "d3", "d4"), scheme = 'add_sequential',  p.adjust = 'BH', seq_stat = .01)

Then in the second round of DIF detection, I planned to use the results from mod1/dif1 to select an anchor and then run another multiGroup model w/ latent mean/variance freed and at least one anchor item, like this: 

mod2 <- multipleGroup(data = df[,c("x2", "x3", "x4", "x5", "x6", "x7, "x8", "x9", "x10")], 1, itemtype = "graded", group = as.character(df[,11]), invariance = c("x1", "free_means", "free_var"), SE = TRUE)

dif2 <- DIF(mod2, c('a', "d1", "d2", "d3", "d4"), scheme = 'add_sequential',  p.adjust = 'BH', seq_stat = .01)

That's good to know the 0x0 df output means no DIF (based on criterion set). I'm wondering though if everything looks okay to you in the code above? When I run the code above, I am able to detect DIF in my mod2/dif2 models. But I always get the 0x0 df output in the mod1/dif1 models, no matter what criterion I set in the dif1 seq_stat (e.g., I even set the seq_stat to a super low bar of .80 and removed the BH adjustment and the 0x0 df output still resulted...Since I'm detecting DIF in mod2/dif2, I wasn't sure if it makes sense that I'm not detecting DIF in mod1/dif1 (which is only being run for the purposes of selecting an anchor anyway)? Or perhaps I am doing something wrong..?

Thank you for your time,
J

On Thu, Sep 5, 2019 at 1:59 PM Phil Chalmers <rphilip....@gmail.com> wrote:
This first warning is one I believe we discussed before, that the latent mean/variance should be freed first after selecting one or more anchor items. Otherwise, you are making the strong assumption that the latent traits have identical distribution properties, which if false will lead to incorrect identification of DIF.

The 0x0 data frame mean that given the first was of DIF searching no DIF items were found according to the selection criteria. HTH.

Phil


On Wed, Sep 4, 2019 at 6:22 PM Jeannie <jeann...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Phil, when I run the DIF function to identify anchor items (example code below), I get the following output: "data frame with 0 columns and 0 rows". 

mod1 <- multipleGroup(data = df[,c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "x5", "x6", "x7, "x8", "x9", "x10")], 1, itemtype = "graded", group = as.character(df[,11]), SE = TRUE)
dif <- DIF(mod1, c('a', "d1", "d2", "d3", "d4"), scheme = 'add_sequential',  p.adjust = 'BH', seq_stat = .01)

After running the first line of code it throws the following warning: "No hyper-parameters were estimated in the DIF model. For effective DIF testing, freeing the focal group hyper-parameters is recommended."

I'm not sure if maybe the DIF function is not working because of this warning? Or does the "data frame with 0 columns and 0 rows" instead mean that no DIF was detected?

Thank you!
Jeannie



On Mon, Aug 26, 2019 at 7:19 AM Phil Chalmers <rphilip....@gmail.com> wrote:

On Sat, Aug 24, 2019 at 12:01 PM Jeannie Brady <jeann...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Phil, I'm reading your 2016 paper "It might not make a big DIF..." (it is awesome by the way). I'd like to use the method you discuss for evaluating DIF but want to be sure I'm translating your method to its programming in mirt correctly. I've copied and pasted your methods and the coding for each step below. Does this look right to you? (this example assumes the test is 10 items and has 5-point response cats). Thank you so much!

1. "To establish a set of potential anchor items, we used a multigroup GRM with no across-group equality constraints as a reference model. 
    mod1 <- multipleGroup(data = df[,c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "x5", "x6", "x7, "x8", "x9", "x10")], 1, itemtype = "graded", group = as.character(df[,11]), invariance = c('free_means', 'free_var'), SE = TRUE)
This looks right except that in the first round we didn't freely estimate the latent mean/variances (these are not identified without anchors). After the first round of the iterations though these were freely estimated. So we basically ran DIF() once to find some probable anchors (assuming the latent trait distributions were equal in the first iteration) and updated the DIF search after that. 

 
2. "Next, likelihood-ratio tests were used to compare the reference model to models that added across-group equality constraints to the a and dk parameters one item at a time. To account for the large number of likelihood ratio tests, we used the multiplicity control method of Benjamini and Hochberg (1995). Based on the DIF analysis, we determined that the third, sixth, seventh, and eighth items were invariant across the two countries. "

dif <- DIF(mod1, c('a', "d1", "d2", "d3", "d4"), scheme = 'add_sequential',  p.adjust = 'BH', seq_stat = .01)

Looks fine.

 

3. "Therefore, these items were used as anchor items in the final multigroup IRT model so that the latent mean and variance parameters in the German group could be estimated. A likelihood-ratio test comparing our final model to a multigroup IRT model with no across-group equality constraints was not statistically significant."
    mod2 <- multipleGroup(data = df[,"x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "x5", "x6", "x7, "x8", "x9", "x10")], 1, itemtype = "graded", group = as.character(df[,11]), invariance = c('x3', 'x6', 'x7', 'x8', 'free_means', 'free_var'), SE = TRUE)
    dif2 <- DIF(mod2, c('a', "d1", "d2", "d3", "d4"), scheme = 'drop',  items2test = c(1:2,4:5,9:10))
Thank you again! -Jeannie

Also looks good.

Phil
 

On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 11:50 AM Phil Chalmers <rphilip....@gmail.com> wrote:
Correct.

Phil


On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 11:48 AM Jeannie Brady <jeann...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Phil, thanks for your reply! If I chose one item as an anchor to identify the model (via the multipleGroup function), then am I correct in my thinking that the "add_sequential" scheme will add additional anchor items to the DIF detection as it loops sequentially over items and identifies items without DIF?  (this is despite the fact that one anchor item might is not ideal as you mentioned) - Jeannie

On Wed, Aug 21, 2019 at 9:33 AM Phil Chalmers <rphilip....@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Jeannie,

You would need to have at least one item's name in the invariance= input to specify an anchor item, otherwise the baseline model will not be sufficiently identified. But, one item is pretty weak in that if you happen to pick an anchor that has DIF then it can throw the results of the search off. I think the common number of anchors in the literature starts with three items, but the more the better. HTH.

Phil


On Tue, Aug 20, 2019 at 9:50 PM Jeannie <jeann...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Phil,

I'm using mirt to test a scale for DIF. I'm using the add sequential scheme and want to be sure I'm identifying my baseline model correctly (code below). I did not enter an anchor item into the "invariance" argument of multiGroup because I am thinking that the purification process performed by the "add_sequential" scheme results in anchor items in each iteration--but I'm not sure if I'm thinking of this correctly and perhaps am identifying my baseline model incorrectly? Any thoughts are appreciated. Thank you! 



mod <- multipleGroup(data = sf.dif[,c("sf1", "sf23", "sf4", "sf5")], 1, 
                                        itemtype = c("2PL", "graded", "2PL", "2PL"), group = as.character(sf.dif[,5]), 
                                        invariance = c('free_means', 'free_var'), SE.type = "Oakes", SE = TRUE)

sf.add.seq <- DIF(mod, c('a', "d", "d1", "d2"), scheme = 'add_sequential', p.adjust = 'BH', seq_stat = .05, plotdif = TRUE) 
print(sf.add.seq)

-Jeannie

out1$adj_pvals

out2 <- DIF(mod_ref, c('a1', 'd'), scheme='add_sequential', items2test = 6:15, p.adjust = 'BH')
